xThreads.title: Terry Tao's Coding Agent Workflow
posts:
1/ How does a Fields medalist use AI to write code? 

Terry Tao just shared his detailed logs on building custom tools using modern coding agents.

Here is what we can learn from his setup: https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/07/11/old-and-new-apps-via-modern-coding-agents/

2/ First, coding agents are highly efficient at generating self-contained helper files (like writing mathematical parser scripts or generating clean regex formatters).

However, they quickly lose context when asked to modify complex, multi-file codebases in a single shot.

3/ To overcome this, Tao recommends an iterative modular approach:

• Keep your components strictly decoupled.
• Have the agent write and test one file at a time.
• Feed compiler errors directly back to the agent rather than trying to fix them manually.

4/ The major takeaway: The bottleneck in software development is no longer writing the code. It is modular system design and error-loop orchestration.

Practitioners should spend more time defining boundaries and less time typing syntax.

xThreads.title: Unifying Neurodegenerative Somatic Damage
posts:
1/ A new study published in Cell has identified a shared somatic mutation pattern across C9ORF72 ALS, C9ORF72 FTD, and Alzheimer’s disease.

This maps a unifying mechanism of neuronal genomic instability: https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(26)00700-2?rss=yes

2/ Key measured results:

• Single-cell whole-genome sequencing of patient brains revealed a shared signature dominated by 2-base pair deletions.
• This damage is driven by aberrant activity of topoisomerase 1 (TOP1) enzymes, specifically linked to oxidative DNA damage.

3/ Why does it matter?

Previously, these neurodegenerative disorders were treated as distinct pathologies. Finding a shared mutagenic driver (TOP1 malfunction) means we can target a single enzyme pathway to prevent DNA damage in multiple diseases.

4/ What should researchers do differently?

Shift therapeutic focus toward designing small-molecule TOP1 stabilizers or reducing neuronal oxidative stress to protect genomic stability rather than just treating downstream protein aggregation (amyloids/tau).

The semiconductor supply chain is undergoing the biggest financing realignment in history.

SK Hynix has raised $26.5B in the largest foreign IPO on record in the United States. Following this listing, U.S. policymakers are actively pushing the memory chip maker to construct domestic production fabs in the country.

### Why it matters:
1. Memory bottlenecks: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the core constraint in scaling AI clusters.
2. Geopolitics: Relying entirely on offshore fabrication leaves the AI industry vulnerable to export shocks.
3. Regional Growth: Subsidies are driving massive infrastructure projects in the US, India, and the Nordics.

### Factual Takeaway:
Semiconductor self-reliance is no longer just a supply-chain strategy; it is a core geopolitical shield. For founders and investors, tracking where these fabs are constructed indicates where high-scale tech hubs will grow over the next decade.

Original coverage: https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/10/sk-hynix-raises-26-5b-in-the-biggest-foreign-ipo-in-us-history-is-urged-to-build-new-us-fabs/

newsletter.title: Terry Tao's Agent Workflows & SK Hynix's $26.5B IPO
newsletter.introduction: Welcome to FutureLoop. Today we dissect the hands-on coding agent logs of a Fields medalist, the massive capital scaling of the AI chip supply chain, and breakthroughs in genomic neurodegeneration research.

stories.title: Terry Tao's Coding Agent Logs
stories.body: Fields medalist Terry Tao published detailed logs using coding agents to build helper scripts. He notes that while agents excel at generating decoupled helper modules, they lose coherence on complex multi-file edits. He recommends keeping code modular and feeding compilation errors directly back to the agent.

stories.title: SK Hynix's $26.5B IPO
stories.body: Memory giant SK Hynix raised $26.5B in a historic US listing to fund HBM chip capacity. US policymakers are now pressing the firm to build manufacturing fabs locally in the US, accelerating the regionalization of high-performance semiconductor supply chains.

stories.title: Mapping Spiking Activity in Visual Cortex
stories.body: A Cell study utilizing Neuropixels probes mapped spiking activity across the mouse visual system during change-detection tasks. The data reveals that visual change detection is governed by adaptation-based visual pathways within strict temporal windows, mapping how sensory and motor signals correlate.

stories.title: NSF Proposes Chinese Collaboration Ban
stories.body: The National Science Foundation drafted policy guidelines that would ban academic collaborations with most Chinese research institutions. This replaces previous risk-mitigation measures with an outright prohibition, significantly impacting global science funding and co-authored paper pipelines.

stories.title: Unifying Mutagenesis Shared in Alzheimer's and ALS
stories.body: Single-cell whole-genome sequencing in Cell identified a shared signature of somatic mutations in ALS, FTD, and Alzheimer's brains. This neuronal genomic damage is driven by aberrant topoisomerase 1 (TOP1) activity linked to oxidative stress, suggesting a unified therapeutic target.

newsletter.takeaway:
Actionable Takeaway:
When building workflows with coding agents, keep modules under 150 lines. Test each module independently, and compile your system using automated integration scripts. Decoupling code prevents context drift in AI model prompts.
